target.title: Support chunked uploads without Content-Length
target.description: Servers that don't set wsgi.input_terminated still send chunked bodies, and returning an empty stream silently drops them. Pass the stream through instead.

summary: This pull request changes `get_input_stream` in werkzeug/wsgi.py to return the input stream directly instead of an empty BytesIO when content_length is None, allowing chunked uploads to be processed.

suspects.title: Infinite stream fallback when safe_fallback is expected
suspects.problem: By removing `io.BytesIO() if safe_fallback else stream` in favor of always returning `stream` when `content_length` is None, callers that rely on `safe_fallback` to prevent hanging on requests without content length or transfer-encoding might now receive an infinite stream and hang workers.
suspects.how_to_check: Search the codebase for usages of `get_input_stream` and check how `safe_fallback` is used or passed across the repository.

Category: reliability

Suspected problem: By removing `io.BytesIO() if safe_fallback else stream` in favor of always returning `stream` when `content_length` is None, callers that rely on `safe_fallback` to prevent hanging on requests without content length or transfer-encoding might now receive an infinite stream and hang workers.

arguments.claim: By removing `io.BytesIO() if safe_fallback else stream` in favor of always returning `stream` when `content_length` is None, `safe_fallback` is ignored and requests without content length return an infinite stream instead of a safe empty fallback.
arguments.explanation: In `get_input_stream`, when `content_length` is None and `wsgi.input_terminated` is not set, the code previously checked `safe_fallback` (defaulting to True) to return an empty `io.BytesIO()` stream, preventing worker hangs on unexpected requests without a content length. The PR replaced this check with an unconditional `return stream`, thereby breaking `safe_fallback` and returning an infinite stream when `content_length` is None.

evidence.note: The code ignores safe_fallback when content_length is None and always returns the raw stream.
The documentation states safe_fallback returns an empty stream when Content-Length is not set, but the code no longer honors safe_fallback here.

arguments.suggested_fix: Restore `return io.BytesIO() if safe_fallback else stream` when content_length is None.
